sourceDocument: The complete user prompt titled Prompt 1 — Bot local de filas da Twitch para Genshin Impact, plus the clarification that application code is organized under apps/web, apps/api, apps/infra and other apps/* as needed.

functional.description: Install and operate one local instance for one Twitch channel with Docker Compose v2, a persistent local PostgreSQL database, one-time persistent bootstrap secrets, migrations before the bot, loopback-only publication by default, health checks, and safe start/stop/update/log instructions.
functional.rationale: The streamer must be able to operate the application without installing Node.js or PostgreSQL, while data and operations survive restarts.

functional.description: Configure Twitch Client ID and Client Secret through a local setup wizard, validate them through Client Credentials, connect the streamer through a session-bound one-time OAuth state, validate token identity/scopes/eligibility, persist refreshes, and support reconnection without exposing credentials.
functional.rationale: The integration must use the streamer's own confidential Twitch application and broadcaster identity.

functional.description: Create, edit, pause/resume, archive, unarchive, and safely delete app-owned channel-points rewards for configurable queues; preserve desired local state separately from confirmed Twitch state and block unsafe broadcaster or client changes.
functional.rationale: A queue's reward and app ownership determine how Twitch redemption operations can safely be managed.

functional.description: Represent configurable queues, unique normalized slugs and aliases, reward settings, UID visibility settings, native Twitch reward limits, lifecycle/sync state, and historical identity without reattaching old history by a reused key.
functional.rationale: The streamer needs multiple independent activities and reliable recovery of their configuration and history.

functional.description: Accept queue entry only from an owned reward redemption or an authorized streamer/moderator manual add; identify people by Twitch user ID, enforce one active entry per user per queue, validate visible-mode UID as exactly nine ASCII digits after trim, and never accept viewer join commands.
functional.rationale: Entry source, identity, and UID policy constrain eligibility and point effects.

functional.description: Maintain waiting, called, in_progress, completed, removed, and no_show entry states through one domain transition service; apply the transition and snapshotted financial policy atomically with ordering, account ownership, audit, and outbox intent.
functional.rationale: All entry mutations need consistent state and point decisions independent of their trigger.

functional.description: Process cancellation and fulfillment intentions from a durable PostgreSQL outbox with stable redemption idempotency, leases, recovery, bounded retry/backoff, rate-limit handling, token-revocation handling, remote-state reconciliation, and visible conflict/unknown outcomes.
functional.rationale: There is no transaction spanning PostgreSQL and Twitch; the application must preserve intent and never claim an unconfirmed financial effect.

functional.description: Subscribe over Twitch EventSub WebSocket to redemption add/update and channel chat messages; send messages through Helix; deduplicate event/message IDs; reconcile reward and redemption state on startup, reconnect, schedule, and operator request.
functional.rationale: The application must receive live events and recover events missed during outages.

functional.description: Parse documented Portuguese queue, account, and management commands as a pure parser separate from execution and authorization; enforce channel, broadcaster/mod badge, optional VIP, actor identity, cooldown, syntax, response-size, and message-send-result rules.
functional.rationale: Chat is an operational surface and untrusted input must not bypass authorization or cause unintended actions.

functional.description: Support queue listing/position/leave, manual add/remove, next/call, start service, complete, move, open/close, archive, clear confirmation, current-account changes, safe call templates, and timeout/no-show behavior as specified.
functional.rationale: These operations form the live queue workflow and must preserve order, point policy, and account ownership.

functional.description: Provide a local Fastify and vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript operator panel and session-protected API for setup, connectivity, queues, entries, financial tasks, reconciliation, account settings, and explicit projections including GET /api/state.
functional.rationale: The streamer needs local operational visibility and controls in addition to chat commands.

functional.description: Persist the current account label, default label, change source, and owning entry; switch automatically only for a one-person next call when enabled and reset to default only when the owner ends.
functional.rationale: Automatic account display must remain attributable to the entry that caused the change.

functional.description: Materialize and expose the complete product identity separately from API contract version and state revision; validate version source consistency and seven-character Git SHA without rewriting release identity during ordinary startup or documentation changes.
functional.rationale: Runtime and build identity must be traceable without making version a mutable startup side effect.

functional.description: Maintain English primary documentation and semantically equivalent Brazilian Portuguese versions for install/use, stories/TDD evidence, integrations, versioning, and user-facing/internal changelogs with reciprocal links.
functional.rationale: Both languages are an explicit collaboration and operation requirement.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a first-run host with Docker Compose v2 and a browser
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user runs docker compose up --build -d or a start script
acceptanceCriteria.then: persistent secrets are bootstrapped once, PostgreSQL becomes healthy, real migrations complete before the non-root bot starts, and the panel is available at the exact loopback-published address without requiring manual configuration edits

acceptanceCriteria.given: a running installation with persisted entries and outbox work
acceptanceCriteria.when: the bot is stopped and recreated or the machine restarts
acceptanceCriteria.then: database and secret volumes persist, tasks recover, the database has no host port, and ordinary scripts never remove volumes

acceptanceCriteria.given: a streamer enters a Client ID and Secret
acceptanceCriteria.when: backend Client Credentials validation fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: the new configuration is not saved and no secret or token is returned or logged

acceptanceCriteria.given: a validated Twitch app and local session
acceptanceCriteria.when: the streamer connects through OAuth
acceptanceCriteria.then: state is random, single-use, short-lived, and session-bound; broadcaster, client, scopes, and channel eligibility are checked before queues are enabled

acceptanceCriteria.given: a configured queue
acceptanceCriteria.when: its reward is created or edited
acceptanceCriteria.then: only an app-owned reward is managed, queue privacy/reward fields are enforced, desired and confirmed remote states remain distinct, and retry never blindly creates a duplicate

acceptanceCriteria.given: a queue deletion is requested
acceptanceCriteria.when: any unfulfilled redemption cancellation is unconfirmed, unknown, or conflicting
acceptanceCriteria.then: reward deletion is not called and the local deletion remains resumable with recovery data

acceptanceCriteria.given: a viewer redeems an owned reward
acceptanceCriteria.when: the event is valid and the queue is open
acceptanceCriteria.then: one waiting entry is created at the end and its position is reported; a rejected, terminal, duplicate, invalid-UID, closed, archived, or deleting redemption creates no active entry and has a durable cancellation intent as specified

acceptanceCriteria.given: manual add is requested
acceptanceCriteria.when: actor, queue lifecycle, target identity, or UID rules fail
acceptanceCriteria.then: the operation creates no entry and causes no point action; hidden-mode UID input is discarded without logging or persistence

acceptanceCriteria.given: an entry transition is requested
acceptanceCriteria.when: the transition is invalid or races another operation
acceptanceCriteria.then: the domain service and database constraints prevent invalid/duplicate state and financial effects; valid terminal operations atomically persist state, audit, policy snapshot, ordering/account changes, and one outbox intent

acceptanceCriteria.given: a next/start/complete/remove/no-show/account operation occurs
acceptanceCriteria.when: concurrent actions or another queue's owner are involved
acceptanceCriteria.then: queue ordering and account ownership remain transactionally consistent, and only the specified owner transition can reset the automatic account change

acceptanceCriteria.given: a financial outbox operation is pending or leased
acceptanceCriteria.when: the process crashes, times out, receives 429/401/5xx, or loses a response
acceptanceCriteria.then: the durable intent remains visible, retries/reconciliation follow the recorded policy, and success is announced only after Twitch confirms the expected terminal status

acceptanceCriteria.given: the remote redemption is already terminal
acceptanceCriteria.when: the observed Twitch status matches or opposes the expected status
acceptanceCriteria.then: matching state resolves the intent without repeating the effect, while opposite or unknowable state is surfaced as conflict/unknown without false refund/consumption claims

acceptanceCriteria.given: EventSub events are repeated, reordered, or lost during disconnection
acceptanceCriteria.when: add/update events and reconciliation overlap
acceptanceCriteria.then: redemption IDs deduplicate, update-before-add terminal history blocks late activation, and partial pagination/failure never removes entries or asserts absence as final proof

acceptanceCriteria.given: the local OAuth token is refreshed, revoked, or loses a required scope
acceptanceCriteria.when: the process starts or periodic validation runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: refreshes persist atomically; affected Twitch sessions pause safely on revocation while the panel, database, and pending work remain available

acceptanceCriteria.given: a chat message resembles a command
acceptanceCriteria.when: it comes from another channel, lacks trusted current-message authorization, duplicates a mutating message ID, or violates syntax/cooldown
acceptanceCriteria.then: no protected mutation or unintended point operation occurs

acceptanceCriteria.given: a valid queue command is executed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the action is a list, position, leave, call, service, move, clear, open/close, or account action
acceptanceCriteria.then: the specified authorization, ordering, confirmation, response-length, send-result, timeout, and financial policy rules are enforced

acceptanceCriteria.given: a browser requests the local panel or API
acceptanceCriteria.when: Host, Origin, session, CSRF, schema, idempotency, or version checks fail
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request is rejected before unauthorized work and no secrets or protected UID are exposed

acceptanceCriteria.given: a local authenticated operator requests state or edits a queue
acceptanceCriteria.when: the current queue UID visibility or lifecycle is considered
acceptanceCriteria.then: only explicit safe projections are returned, current privacy controls govern output, and stale/incompatible mutations fail safely

acceptanceCriteria.given: version files are validated or a build is materialized
acceptanceCriteria.when: Git metadata is missing, valid, malformed, or lookup fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: the documented marker is used only when Git is unavailable, materialized SHA has exactly seven hex characters from the exact source commit, and ordinary checks do not rewrite product version files

acceptanceCriteria.given: a requirement, policy, script, or evidence changes
acceptanceCriteria.when: documentation is updated
acceptanceCriteria.then: the English primary and Portuguese equivalent preserve paths, commands, IDs, dates, outputs, and meaning, with reciprocal links and no contradictory policy

nonFunctional.description: Bind each installation to one broadcaster ID and one Twitch client ID; protect credentials and restrict Twitch sessions after revocation or scope loss.
nonFunctional.metric: Zero client secrets, access/refresh tokens, authorization codes, database passwords, or connection strings in HTTP responses, UI URLs, logs, chat, or raw persisted event payloads.

nonFunctional.description: Keep the local control plane private by default with loopback publication, exact Host/Origin checks, local sessions, CSRF protection, safe OAuth callback rules, and no implicit proxy trust.
nonFunctional.metric: Mutation requests fail without valid session and CSRF; non-allowlisted Host/Origin and rebinding attempts are rejected before administrative handlers.

nonFunctional.description: Persist all domain state, audit, and pending work in PostgreSQL and recover safely across process, network, and machine interruptions.
nonFunctional.metric: No active financial intent or leased operation is lost after restart; recovery behavior is tested with real PostgreSQL migrations.

nonFunctional.description: Treat Twitch as authority for points and PostgreSQL as authority for local order, service state, intent, and history; do not claim exactly-once network execution.
nonFunctional.metric: All terminal redemption outcomes resolve by confirmed remote status, or remain explicitly pending/conflicted/unknown.

nonFunctional.description: Support multiple queues in a single channel with queue-local atomic ordering and globally serialized current-account mutations while running one bot instance.
nonFunctional.metric: Concurrent tests preserve one active user per queue, queue order, no cross-queue movement, and account ownership; multi-instance scaling is out of scope.

nonFunctional.description: Treat chat and redemption text as untrusted; persist only allowlisted fields and render user-controlled text safely.
nonFunctional.metric: No raw invalid input or full chat/redemption payload is persisted; output uses text rendering and never echoes rejected content.

nonFunctional.description: Provide clear pt-BR chat, help, and panel operation, while technical identifiers, logs, database names, and event names remain English.
nonFunctional.metric: All user-facing live operations are in pt-BR, responses are at most 500 characters, and errors explain a safe next action.

nonFunctional.description: Installation requires Docker Compose v2 and a browser, and scripts handle browser opening with an address fallback.
nonFunctional.metric: No host Node.js, PostgreSQL, compiler, or manual .env/YAML edits are required for first run.

nonFunctional.description: Use JavaScript ESM with JSDoc, Fastify, vanilla web assets, Prisma, PostgreSQL, pinned dependencies, npm lockfile, and Vitest without application TypeScript, transpilation, or bundling.
nonFunctional.metric: `package.json` declares ESM, dependencies are pinned and locked, and application source contains no TypeScript or frontend build pipeline.

nonFunctional.description: Keep English documentation canonical and Portuguese documentation equivalent, and record genuine TDD evidence per behavioral increment.
nonFunctional.metric: Every completed increment lists observed Red, Green, Refactor, commands, and affected file list in both stories documents.

nonFunctional.description: Use short database transactions and perform all Twitch network calls outside database transactions; prevent aggressive retry loops.
nonFunctional.metric: No database transaction remains open across a Twitch API call; retry delay uses backoff/jitter and respects API rate-limit headers.

nonFunctional.description: Run the bot container without root privileges, mount only necessary secrets read-only, exclude local operational secrets and data from source control/build context, and explain local data sensitivity.
nonFunctional.metric: Container process UID is non-root, secret access is least-privilege, and `.env`, local secrets, dumps, and database artifacts are ignored.

constraints.description: Application source is JavaScript ESM with type=module and JSDoc; no TypeScript application code, transpiler, bundler, or frontend build is allowed.
constraints.impact: Runtime libraries and test strategy must support direct JavaScript execution.

constraints.description: Use Fastify and @fastify/static, vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript, compatible @twurple/auth, @twurple/api, @twurple/eventsub-ws, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Docker Compose v2, Vitest, package-lock.json, and npm ci.
constraints.impact: No hosted ORM/database, SQLite, alternate web framework, or queue service may replace the selected stack.

constraints.description: Repository application layout uses apps/web, apps/api, apps/infra, and other apps/* as needed; .env.example is framework scaffolding and not the product configuration source.
constraints.impact: Runtime components must live under the apps/* monorepo structure and documentation must not adopt framework example environment values as product configuration.

constraints.description: Use Prisma ORM 6 with prisma-client-js while supported by the selected stable v6 release, prisma.config.mjs, matching CLI/client versions, and PostgreSQL driver adapter packages; Prisma 7 prisma-client output is TypeScript and cannot meet the JavaScript-only source requirement.
constraints.impact: Version pin and generator compatibility must be verified in official Prisma documentation and dependency metadata.

constraints.description: One installation serves exactly one broadcaster and one Twitch app; no hosted backend, remote database, telemetry, public-domain requirement, second bot account, multi-channel mode, or horizontal replication.
constraints.impact: Data and credentials stay local; Twitch is the only required runtime external service.

constraints.description: No Discord/DM integration, viewer join command, public signup, UID account registration, OBS overlay, rankings, backup/export product feature, or chat integration via IRC/@twurple/chat.
constraints.impact: Only specified Twitch redemption/manual entry and local panel operations are in scope.

constraints.description: Financial effects use PostgreSQL outbox plus Twitch confirmation; no external queue broker and no exactly-once network promise.
constraints.impact: All mutations must persist intent before API calls and expose pending/conflict/unknown states.

constraints.description: Default product/runtime identity starts at base 0.1.0, release stage alpha, and pre-Git marker v0.1.0-0000000-alpha; only @devops owns release/tag operations and stage promotion requires explicit human approval.
constraints.impact: Normal commits, tests, docs edits, and startup cannot increment or rewrite release identity.

constraints.description: Main project documentation is English with equivalent Brazilian Portuguese copies and reciprocal links; product interface/help/chat remains pt-BR.
constraints.impact: Affected documentation must be updated in both languages in the same increment.

constraints.description: Implement TDD before each behavior change, use actual isolated PostgreSQL for persistence guarantees, and record observed evidence without inventing runs.
constraints.impact: No story can be called done with missing Red/Green/Refactor evidence or unverified integration guarantees.

assumptions.description: The GitHub repository owner is the currently authenticated account and the repository name is derived from this project directory, `subarushogun_gi_twich_bot`.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: The private repository could be created under the wrong owner or name.

assumptions.description: The user's latest folder-layout clarification supersedes the earlier initial generic layout and requires application components under apps/*.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Generated project paths and architecture could diverge from the user's intended repository structure.

assumptions.description: A local browser and Docker Compose v2 are available to the operator; Twitch developer registration and authorized credentials are supplied later by the streamer.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Live OAuth/API validation cannot be demonstrated until those prerequisites exist.

states.error: Show actionable local instruction without secrets
states.empty: Show Twitch setup wizard and no default/example reward

flow: show exact callback and Twitch developer console link
validate pair without persisting on failure

states.error: Explain corrective action without raw technical errors or credentials
states.empty: Show not-connected state while keeping panel/database available

flow: verify managed reward and redemption identity/status
persist entry or rejection and outbox operation

states.loading: No viewer-facing spinner; durable operation is pending
states.error: No raw input echo; disclose requested/pending/confirmed financial state
states.empty: If no queue accepts the reward, cancel durably and explain safe next step

interactions.trigger: Streamer operates a queue from chat or panel
flow: execute the single domain transition service

states.empty: Explain when queue/list/selection has no entries

edgeCases.scenario: A Twitch reward create request times out after the remote create may have succeeded.
edgeCases.handling: Query app-managed rewards before retry; if ownership/association remains unprovable, stop automatic retries and require panel resolution.

edgeCases.scenario: A redemption update arrives before its add event or an event repeats after reconnect.
edgeCases.handling: Persist/dedupe by redemption ID and terminal observation so late add cannot create an active entry.

edgeCases.scenario: PostgreSQL commits local intent but process exits before or during the Twitch request.
edgeCases.handling: Recover through durable outbox lease, query remote status when outcome is uncertain, and never claim exactly-once delivery.

edgeCases.scenario: Reward deletion is requested while rejected or unimported UNFULFILLED redemptions exist.
edgeCases.handling: Enumerate all pages, cancel each, verify no pending redemptions, and defer reward DELETE until confirmed because Twitch may fulfill remaining redemptions on delete.

edgeCases.scenario: Two simultaneous redemptions or commands attempt to create/modify an active entry for the same viewer and queue.
edgeCases.handling: Use PostgreSQL uniqueness and queue transaction serialization; convert expected uniqueness race into a durable cancellation outcome for duplicate redemption.

edgeCases.scenario: UID input is invalid, contains secrets or additional text, or a queue changes from visible to hidden while notifications are pending.
edgeCases.handling: Do not retain raw input; clear persisted queue UIDs on hide; render queued notification from current privacy settings at send time.

edgeCases.scenario: Twitch token is revoked, loses scope, or broadcaster is not affiliate/partner.
edgeCases.handling: Pause Twitch-dependent operations, preserve database and outbox, keep local panel alive, and explain reconnection/eligibility action.

edgeCases.scenario: EventSub disconnect or paginated Helix reconciliation fails part way through.
edgeCases.handling: Resume SDK reconnect protocol where available, reconcile after real disconnect, and never treat partial results or absence from a page as a terminal state.

edgeCases.scenario: A timed call was not confirmed sent or the viewer started service while the timeout job is firing.
edgeCases.handling: Start deadline only after send confirmation and serialize timeout with state transition so in-progress entries cannot become no-show.

edgeCases.scenario: A local request supplies an unexpected Host/Origin, malicious markup, stale revision, or missing CSRF token.
edgeCases.handling: Reject before mutating work; use explicit schemas, safe projections, text rendering, session/CSRF and exact origin protections.

edgeCases.scenario: An old outbox notification still contains a UID after visibility was changed.
edgeCases.handling: Do not store rendered sensitive text as authoritative; reconstruct message at send time from current queue settings and entry data, clearing UIDs when hidden.

edgeCases.scenario: A local reward slug is reused after deletion while history/outbox remains linked to the old queue.
edgeCases.handling: Use immutable local queue IDs for history and operation references; never associate by a matching slug/title.

terminology.definition: A local participant record in a queue, regardless of manual or reward source.
A Twitch Channel Points redemption with its own remote ID and status; a rejected redemption also remains tracked without a local Entry.
The application has durably requested Twitch CANCELED; points are refunded only after Twitch confirms that status.
The application has durably requested Twitch FULFILLED; consumption is confirmed only after Twitch reports that status.
The queue has no reward text input and does not accept, store, or disclose UID values.
A plain-text label shown for the live game's account; it is not a game login or credential.

openQuestions.question: None currently block architecture: all product decisions and acceptance rules are specified by the user. Validate real Twitch behavior later with authorized credentials; report that integration as pending until it occurs.
